title: Dalitz plot binning optimization for the model-independent measurement of the CKM angle $β$ with $B^0 \to D π^+ π^-$, $D \to K_S^0 π^+ π^-$ decays
comment: 23 pages, 12 figures, 5 tables. Machine-readable nominal TD binning and a Python reader are included as ancillary files
summary: A model-independent measurement of the CKM angle $β$ can be performed using a time-dependent analysis of $B^0 \to D π^+ π^-$, $D \to K_S^0 π^+ π^-$ decays, where the Dalitz plots of both the $B$ and $D$ decays are divided into bins. The choice of binning scheme for the $B^0 \to D π^+ π^-$ Dalitz plot directly impacts the statistical sensitivity to $β$. This paper presents an optimization of this binning using a Fisher information-based quality factor $Q^2$ and simulated annealing. The optimized binning improves the sensitivity to $β$ by approximately $10\%$ relative to the equal-phase-difference baseline, as validated by toy Monte Carlo studies without experimental effects. The robustness of this improvement against decay time acceptance, Dalitz plot efficiency, Dalitz plot resolution, and background contributions is also assessed.

title: Large mass-ratio ($3< q \leq 10$) inspiral-merger-ringdown model for eccentric binary black holes
summary: We present $\texttt{EccHybIMR22}$, a fully analytical $\textbf{Ecc}$entric-$\textbf{Hyb}$rid-$\textbf{I}$nspiral-$\textbf{M}$erger-$\textbf{R}$ingdown model for the quadrupole ($\ell$=$2$, $|m|$=$2$ or simply the $\textbf{22}$) mode. The model is obtained by smoothly attaching an eccentric-inspiral to a quasi-circular-merger-ringdown prescription and is trained on eccentric numerical relativity (NR) simulations with mass ratios $q\leq 10$. In particular, we focus on obtaining a model that is sensitive to large mass ratios ($q>3$). Leveraging the recent expansion of SXS catalog of NR simulations, we construct a set of 91 hybrids (obtained by combining waveforms from post-Newtonian (PN) theory with NR simulations) with a target low total mass limit ($M_{\rm low}$) of $20M_{\odot}$ at an averaged 22 mode frequency of 20Hz, inaccessible with existing NR simulations alone. Employing a little less than a third of these hybrids as targets, we construct $\texttt{EccHybIMR22}$ and recover $65\%$ of the hybrids from the remaining set with mismatches smaller than $\sim3\%$ for a total mass of $40M_\odot$ (chosen arbitrarily) and orbital eccentricity $e_{\rm 20Hz}\lesssim0.33$ ($e_{\rm 20Hz}\lesssim 0.12$) for mass ratios $q\leq3$ ($q>3$). Furthermore, when tested against 175 SXS simulations, the model is able to recover nearly $80\%$ of the simulations with similar mismatches for systems with $0\lesssim e^{\rm NR}_{\rm 20Hz}\lesssim 0.3$.

title: Dynamical BEC formation and vanishing entropy for trapped bosons in non-relativistic QED via nonlinear resonance cascades
summary:
The dynamical formation of a complete Bose-Einstein condensate and the asymptotic purification of trapped bosons coupled to a quantized radiation field are rigorously established. By tracking the macroscopic one-particle density matrix $κ_T$ through a nonlinear resonance cascade, it is demonstrated that radiative relaxation irreversibly depletes all excited trap modes, even when the initial macroscopic state $κ_0$ is genuinely mixed. Here $κ_T$ is an average, with respect to a de Finetti measure $μ_0$, over mean-field particle-field orbits, so that the mixedness of $κ_0$ reflects a statistical ensemble of orbits. Under the assumptions of a non-vanishing initial ground state component and strictly positive downward Fermi-Golden-Rule rates, strong trace-norm convergence to a pure condensate is proven, $$
  \lim_{T\to\infty} \| κ_T-|χ_0\rangle\langleχ_0| \|_{\mathfrak{S}_1(\mathfrak{h})} = 0 \, . $$ Furthermore, the von Neumann entropy of the macroscopic one-particle density matrix is shown to vanish asymptotically, $$
  \lim_{T\to\infty}S[κ_T]=0 \, , $$ without any claim of monotonicity in $T$. Thus, any initially mixed, positive-entropy state ($0<S[κ_0]<\infty$) is purified to the ground state $|χ_0\rangle\langleχ_0|$. For the proof, we derive the Hartree hierarchy of the coupled system of bosons and photons from the finite-$N$ BBGKY hierarchy of the microscopic quantum many-body system, establishing trace-norm convergence in the mean-field limit as $N\to\infty$. The limits are taken successively; first $N\to\infty$, then the weak-coupling limit, and finally $T\to\infty$. Although the global particle-field evolution remains unitary, the macroscopic one-particle state converges to a pure state as energy and correlations are continuously radiated into the dispersive field.

title: Axionic Casimir Torque
summary: In the canonical Casimir effect, the quantum vacuum is isotropic, and the minimization of vacuum energy drives only a linear attractive force between the plates. However, the introduction of an axion gradient breaks this rotational symmetry. It can be demonstrated that these asymmetric zero-point fluctuations exert a macroscopic mechanical twist on the plates proportional to $\vec{b}^2 \sin (2\vartheta)$ where $\vec{b}$ is the spatial axion gradient and $\vartheta$ is the angle between the axion gradient and the normal to the plates.

title: Microscopic entropy of regular BTZ black holes in 3d Lovelock gravity at all orders
summary: We give a microscopic derivation of the semi-classical entropy of the black holes of 3d Lovelock gravity with an infinite tower of regularized Lovelock corrections, which include the regular BTZ black holes found recently. Working in the mini-superspace formalism, we show that the reduced action and its boundary term can be obtained in closed form at all orders in terms of the generating function of the couplings. Assuming the ground state is described by the soliton obtained from the static black hole by a double Wick rotation, we compute the soliton mass and reproduce the semi-classical entropy from the Cardy formula without central charges for arbitrary couplings. We then extend the mini-superspace to stationary configurations, compute the mass and the angular momentum of the rotating black holes obtained by a boost, and verify the Cardy formula in the presence of rotation.

title: Conserved-charge diffusion in hot and dense QCD matter
comment: 11 pages, 7 captioned figures. Submitted for publication
summary: We study the coupled diffusion of baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness in hot and dense quark matter using a three-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model with self-consistently generated constituent quark masses. The complete diffusion matrix is evaluated within a relaxation-time kinetic approach, including its diagonal and off-diagonal components. We find that the off-diagonal transport coefficients exhibit distinct temperature and baryon-chemical-potential dependence associated with the flavor-dependent composition of the charge carriers. We further investigate generalized charge diffusivities and mobilities obtained from the corresponding susceptibilities. At finite baryon chemical potential, the baryon and strangeness mobility scales cross, reflecting the different density dependence of their transport coefficients and susceptibilities. The results provide model benchmarks for coupled conserved-charge transport in baryon-rich QCD matter.

title: Quasibound states of charged Dirac fields around Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg black holes
summary: We study quasibound states of a massive charged Dirac field on the Einstein--Euler--Heisenberg (EEH) black hole, the extension of Reissner--Nordström (RN) by the leading weak-field vacuum-polarization term of QED. We derive the background to first order in the Euler--Heisenberg coupling $a$. We show that it admits a nondegenerate horizon at $Q=M$ and an extremal charge $Q_{\rm ext}=M[1+a/(40M^2)+\mathcal{O}(a^2)]>M$, with horizon data that depend on $\sqrt a$ near extremality. From the separated radial equations, we derive an identity that excludes real-frequency quasibound states on any background of this class, so damped branches cannot become unstable. Since the EEH corrections first enter at $\mathcal{O}(r^{-5})$ in the electrostatic potential, the trapping condition $Mμ^2-qQω_R>0$ and the hydrogenic spectrum coincide with RN, and no fine-structure-order splitting arises. Two-sided shooting with a Muller root finder shows that the real frequencies shift only by near-zone amounts that are linear in $a$ and strongly suppressed with angular momentum. The damping rates respond in a branch-dependent way. At $Q/M=0.99$ the $\ell=0$ ground state becomes slightly longer-lived, while the $(n_r,j,\ell,λ)=(0,\tfrac32,1,-2)$ state decays up to $80\%$ faster for $a/M^2\le1$, and near the trapping threshold the damping rate increases by up to $60\%$. Switching on the metric and potential corrections separately, together with a WKB analysis of the inner barrier, identifies the mechanisms: Coulomb screening always increases leakage, while the metric correction controls the sign and size of the $\ell$-dependent effect. Characteristic time-domain evolutions with Richardson-extrapolated matrix-pencil extraction reproduce the frequency-domain shifts.

title: Spectral Theory of an Exactly Solvable Quantum-Optical Oscillator
summary:
We study a one-dimensional single-excitation model of a scalar photon field coupled to a continuum of two-level atoms with quadratic density. The resulting matrix Hamiltonian has an unbounded spatially varying coupling and is not semibounded. We prove that it is essentially self-adjoint and determine its spectrum explicitly. The continuous spectrum is the half-line $(-\infty,Ω]$, where $Ω$ is the atomic resonance frequency, while the spectrum above $Ω$ consists of a strictly increasing sequence of simple eigenvalues. These eigenvalues are characterized by the interlaced zeros of the Airy function and its derivative and satisfy \begin{align*}
  ω_n = \left(\frac{3πg n}{4}\right)^{1/2} + \fracΩ{4} + O(n^{-1/2}). \end{align*} The analysis is based on a nonlinear spectral reduction that yields a confining massless relativistic oscillator above $Ω$ and an inverted oscillator below $Ω$.

title: Dalitz plot binning optimization for the model-independent measurement of the CKM angle $β$ with $B^0 \to D π^+ π^-$, $D \to K_S^0 π^+ π^-$ decays
comment: 23 pages, 12 figures, 5 tables. Machine-readable nominal TD binning and a Python reader are included as ancillary files
summary: A model-independent measurement of the CKM angle $β$ can be performed using a time-dependent analysis of $B^0 \to D π^+ π^-$, $D \to K_S^0 π^+ π^-$ decays, where the Dalitz plots of both the $B$ and $D$ decays are divided into bins. The choice of binning scheme for the $B^0 \to D π^+ π^-$ Dalitz plot directly impacts the statistical sensitivity to $β$. This paper presents an optimization of this binning using a Fisher information-based quality factor $Q^2$ and simulated annealing. The optimized binning improves the sensitivity to $β$ by approximately $10\%$ relative to the equal-phase-difference baseline, as validated by toy Monte Carlo studies without experimental effects. The robustness of this improvement against decay time acceptance, Dalitz plot efficiency, Dalitz plot resolution, and background contributions is also assessed.

title: Testing Minimal $U(2)^3$ Right-Handed Flavor Breaking in a Singlet-Scalar Vector-Like Quark Portal
summary: We study a portal of a $Z_2$-odd singlet scalar and a vector like down quark, in which a right handed flavor breaking spurion extends the portal coupling from $b_R$ to $d_R$ and $s_R$. This single coupling vector links the $b\to s$, $b\to d$, and $s\to d$ transitions. We compute the one loop dipole and $ΔF=2$ Wilson coefficients, and show that a real scalar generates no $ΔF=2$ amplitude at one loop. Using a seven observable profile likelihood of $B$ meson mixing, $ε_K$, and radiative decays, with the CKM, lattice, and short distance inputs treated as nuisance parameters, we compare a generic spurion, minimal $U(2)^3$ with a free size of the light quark couplings, and a CKM-aligned ansatz. We have found that the present data cannot yet test the flavor structure: the Standard Model is compatible with the data, with a pseudo experiment $p$-value of $0.20$, and no direction of the light quark couplings can be excluded at 95% CL. For $M_D\simeq m_{\mathcal{S}}=1$ TeV and $|λ_b|=1$, the relative light quark coupling $ε_R$ is bounded at 95% CL by $0.227$ for a generic spurion and by $0.211$ for minimal $U(2)^3$. More precise measurements of the $B_s$ mixing phase at the LHC and of $\sin2β$ at LHCb and Belle-II, together with improved lattice and CKM inputs, can make the minimality of the flavor structure testable if a deviation from the Standard Model is observed.

title: Random wave chaos on momentum-fractionated microstate geometries
summary: We study the role of momentum fractionation in the development of chaos on smooth 3-charge supergravity solutions of D1-D5 theory, specifically momentum-fractionated superstrata. We probe the chaos through the dynamics of null geodesics and waves. On fractionated backgrounds, both geodesics and waves show uniformly strong chaos (large chaotic sea and near-perfect agreement with the Berry random wave hypothesis). In contrast, geodesics and waves on single-mode (non-fractionated) superstrata are closer to separability (although still chaotic). We discuss a possibility that such dichotomy can be related to the expectation that monotone BPS states are less chaotic than fortuitous ones. Finally, we explain why our chaos probes are meaningful for microstate geometries even though they become trivial in the black hole limit.

title: Event Generation for Neutrino and Muon DIS at the LHC
summary: Neutrinos and muons produced in the forward direction of LHC collisions and detected by the FASER and SND@LHC experiments enable a comprehensive deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) programme, covering both neutral and charged currents, at TeV energies. This programme aims to provide stringent constraints on proton and nuclear structure as well as on hadron fragmentation, and to offer novel insight into neutrino interactions at the highest energies achieved in a laboratory. Realising this potential requires accurate and precise simulations of neutral- and charged-current DIS. We systematically compare the predictions of NLO general-purpose Monte Carlo (MC) event generators for neutrino- and muon-initiated DIS at the LHC (Sherpa, Herwig7, and POWHEG) against analytical structure-function calculations (YADISM) and dedicated neutrino simulation packages (GENIE, NuWro, GiBUU). Within this framework, we quantify the role of higher-order QCD corrections, (nuclear) parton distribution functions (PDFs), parton shower and hadronisation modelling, and QED radiation both for inclusive observables and for the FASER fiducial selections. We also present representative applications to the FASER neutrino programme: comparisons with its most recent data from the emulsion and electronic sub-detectors, a study of strange PDF sensitivity in the dimuon final state, and predictions for charged-hadron production in semi-inclusive DIS. Our analysis highlights the agreement of modern event generators for inclusive and differential DIS observables once common settings are adopted, while differences remain for observables sensitive to the hadronic final state.

title: Bartnik's splitting conjecture and the cosmological wall: a Cauchy Busemann function approach
summary: Bartnik's conjecture states that a timelike geodesically complete cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition splits as a static product. We show that any counterexample exhibits a peculiar global causal structure: two disjoint open regions, the future and the past cosmological developments, separated by a non-empty closed causally convex set: the cosmological wall. The developments are bounded by $C^0$ null hypersurfaces, the cosmological horizons, and a component of each horizon contains a lightlike line. These objects are natural and hence carry physical significance, as they do not depend on the choice of Cauchy hypersurface. They can be defined through the Cauchy Busemann functions $b^\pm$ of a compact Cauchy hypersurface $Σ$, the developments being their finiteness domains. Using a product trick we show that $b^+$ is the graph function of a Cauchy horizon in $M\times \mathbb{R}$, and so inherits the regularity and dynamical properties of horizons: $b^+$ is continuous, locally Lipschitz and locally semi-concave on its finiteness domain, and its calibrated curves are timelike rays. We prove that if the two cosmological developments intersect, which happens whenever $b^+$ is $C^1$ on its finiteness domain, then the spacetime contains a timelike line and hence splits, a result which recovers several positive results of the literature. We also obtain a localized rigidity version of Hawking's singularity theorem: if some compact Cauchy hypersurface has non-positive mean curvature on the future development, the spacetime splits. Hence, in a counterexample, every compact Cauchy hypersurface expands somewhere in the future development and contracts somewhere in the past one. If the wall has empty interior, it coincides with both horizons and is ruled by lightlike lines, and under null completeness its components are smooth totally geodesic null hypersurfaces.

title: Haagerup-Izumi modular data from hyperbolic words: S-fold TQFTs, central charge, torsion and the Bethe vacua
summary:
The modular data of the doubles of the Haagerup--Izumi categories is a grafting of two finite metric groups (conjectured by Evans--Gannon, proved for untwisted categories by Gannon--Schopieray--Yadav). Gang and Kim found non-unitary modular data of this shape in the topological twist of rank-$0$ $S$-fold theories, from the Bethe vacua of an abelianised gauge theory. The aim is to understand rigorously the significance of the handle-gluing and fibering operators, and to construct the Bethe vacua.
  For every hyperbolic once-punctured-torus monodromy $\varphi$, a word in $L$ and $R$, the two groups are $A_\mp=\coker(\varphi\mp1)$, with the torsion linking forms of the mapping tori of $\varphi$ and $-\varphi$. Over all words of trace $m^2+2$ these forms reproduce the Evans--Gannon table of Q-systems, one printed entry being corrected, and the distinct modular data in the list of Gannon--Schopieray--Yadav. The Bethe data are given in closed form by the word: the level matrix, the positive vacuum, $c_{\eff}=\#L$, and the handle-gluing values $2^{\#L}λ^{\pm1}|A_-||A_+|$ at the identity classes, $λ$ the stretch factor. Each kernel vector of $\varphi\mp1$ modulo $|A_\mp|$ at which an explicit trigonometric formula does not vanish gives a solution of the Bethe equations in closed form. Under the half-index dictionary, with the unit in the class of $σV^*$, $c\equiv\#L-6\#R\pmod{24}$.

title: Probing LZ-Motivated TeV Higgsino Dark Matter through Heavier Sparticles at LHC
summary: The nearly pure TeV-scale Higgsino dark matter provides a natural explanation for the high-energy nuclear-recoil excess reported by LUX-ZEPLIN. Such a heavy and compressed Higgsino spectrum makes direct searches at the LHC challenging. We therefore investigate complementary probes through the production and decay of heavier sparticles. We perform a comprehensive analysis and obtain the following observations: (i) For a TeV Higgsino, the current LHC Run-2 searches exclude gluino up to approximately 2.2~TeV, while the HL-LHC can give an exclusion reach of 2.5--2.6~TeV and a discovery reach of 2.3--2.4~TeV; (ii) The light-flavor squark coannihilation window lies beyond the Run-2 reach, but its lower end could be excluded at the HL-LHC under optimistic assumptions; (iii) The Run-2 search does not exclude the stop or sbottom benchmarks; (iv) The slepton and heavier-electroweakino productions are too small to access at the HL-LHC.

title: Symmetric Dual Breather Modes as a Dynamic Origin of Tiny Particle Masses
summary: Spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) is conventionally understood through static vacuum selection in low-energy approximations. However, the nonperturbative dynamical pathways connecting symmetric configurations to asymmetric states remain an open question. In this paper, we propose an operator-theoretic framework that characterizes $Z_{2}$ symmetry breaking in scalar field theory through spectral branching. Specifically, we identify an effective invariant manifold of the nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation termed the "symmetric dual breather mode," whose phase-space geometry is traced using a $t$-dependent finite-dimensional representation. Our analysis demonstrates that static SSB represents merely a small-amplitude limit ($A \ll φ_{v1}$). As the amplitude increases into the heteroclinic regime ($A > φ_{v1}$), the field dynamically overflows the central barrier, yielding a vanishing time-averaged order parameter ($\langle φ\rangle = 0$) and driving a geometric curvature cancellation ($\langle V''(φ) \rangle_{t} \to 0$). Governed by a universal scaling function $\mathfrak{F}(y)$, the logarithmic period divergence near the heteroclinic boundary naturally generates sub-eV effective mass scales without fine-tuning bare parameters. Furthermore, this dynamic barrier overflow naturally favors Majorana-like self-conjugate states over Dirac-type states. Additionally, nonlinear phase interference along the heteroclinic channel induces asymmetric phase-space contraction, decoupling the right-handed mode and dynamically giving rise to the left-handed Weyl equation. These results bridge nonperturbative wave dynamics, topological mass suppression, chiral selection, and the dynamic origin of active neutrino masses.

title: Charged Lepton Flavor Violation: A Theory Overview
comment: 15 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. Contribution to CLFV 2026 proceedings
summary: We present a theory-oriented overview of the significance of charged-lepton flavor violation -- one of the cleanest windows onto physics beyond the Standard Model. We also summarize the current experimental landscape and illustrate how different measurements can diagnose the underlying new physics.

title: Vanishing Love Numbers of Kerr-Newman Black Holes
summary: Tidal Love numbers characterize the conservative response of compact objects to external perturbations and provide a powerful probe of their nature. While the static Love numbers of Schwarzschild, Kerr, and Reissner--Nordström black holes remarkably vanish, the tidal response of a generic Kerr--Newman black hole has remained unexplored due to the intrinsic coupling between gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations. Exploiting a recent breakthrough in the separability of these perturbations, we analytically determine the static tidal response of the most general stationary black hole in four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory. For arbitrary multipole order, charge, and spin, we show that the entire matrix of conservative Love numbers vanishes, including the mixed gravito-electromagnetic couplings. We also compute the nonvanishing static dissipative response induced by frame dragging.

title: Inverse eigenvalue problem for discrete three-diagonal Schroedinger operator and the continuum limit in Tikhonov regularization approach
summary: In the present article the self-contained derivation of main formulas of the inverse eigenvalue problem for the Sturm-Liouville operator is given on the base of its discrete approximation and the subsequent transition to the limit of the continuum coordinate. In doing so, we adhere to Tikhonov concept, where the discrete approximation is performed as a regularization of the ill-posed operator problem. While the continuum limit for the three-diagonal matrix Hamiltonian is impossible as such, following the Tikhonov procedure leads not to a limit for the potential matrix itself, but rather for a certain combination of the matrix elements, and this limit is precisely the desired potential in the continuum case.

title: Nonequilibrium framework for first-order phase transitions
summary: The first-order phase transition is central to electroweak baryogenesis and gravitational wave generation, yet thermal equilibrium effective potential analyses cannot describe the real-time non-equilibrium dynamics of the phase transition process. We use the Schwinger-Keldysh closed-time-path formalism of real-time finite-temperature field theory to study these effects. For the $φ^6$ model, we derive the effective action and the corresponding Langevin equation. We further extend the formalism to the two scalar fields case, obtaining the coupled Langevin equations. These results provide a theoretical framework for the bubble nucleation simulation of the non-equilibrium phase transition process, laying the foundation for reliable predictions of baryogenesis and gravitational wave signals.

title: Relativistic Covariance from Hamiltonian Hydrodynamics in the Chiral Limit
summary: We derive the covariant equations of nondissipative chiral hydrodynamics from their equal-time Hamiltonian formulation and identify the Lie--Poisson structure implicit in the chiral brackets. This structure combines fluid motion with local chiral transformations. For a parity-invariant Hamiltonian quadratic in chiral charge densities and pion gradients, without external backgrounds, we derive and solve the constraints imposed by Lorentz boosts. Their coupled nonlinear sector is equivalent to the linear boost transformation laws of a symmetric tensor, which determine the velocity dependence from rest-frame data. For finite, positive rest-frame coefficients, finite ordinary-fluid energy density and thermodynamic derivatives, and a momentum--velocity relation that can be solved in either direction, the chiral Hamiltonian coefficients remain finite at every fluid speed below light speed if and only if the rest-frame pion propagation speed does not exceed the speed of light. This formulation makes symmetry constraints explicit and provides a starting point for future thermodynamically consistent dissipative extensions.

title: Implications for new physics solutions to the LSND and MiniBooNE anomalies after MicroBooNE results
summary: Over the past couple of decades, the Liquid Scintillator Neutrino Detector (LSND) and MiniBooNE (MB) neutrino experiments have provided statistically significant evidence of persistent and as yet unexplained electron-like event excesses. The MicroBooNE experiment, with sensitive particle identification capabilities designed to shed light on these anomalous results, has conducted a number of analyses to test whether the excess is due to photons, electrons or $e^+e^-$ pair productions, all of which give almost identical signals in LSND and MB. Recent MicroBooNE searches, in addition to checking Standard Model (SM) processes, have focused on proposed new physics scenarios involving new mediators and dark portals beyond the SM. We study the consequences and effects of these analyses for the many theoretical proposals put forth to generate the three types of signals above in order to understand the observed excesses. We discuss which classes of solutions are allowed, disallowed or require further scrutiny involving theoretical and experimental efforts. We give an example of a new solution that survives the restrictions imposed by MicroBooNE results and other existing bounds. We point out that a light ($m\leq 30$ MeV) dark neutral spin zero mediator with dominantly pseudoscalar couplings, decaying to an $e^+e^-$ pair, can account for the observations. We indicate that if such a model is realised, it may point to the possibility that neutrinos are Dirac particles, and that there are dark Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs) of mass ${\cal O}(100)$ MeV. We discuss issues related to CP violation and ultra-violet completion of these models. Finally we stress that a search for the excess in incoherent scattering channels in MicroBooNE and SBND could help clarify the physics behind these persistent anomalies.

title: Null-Energy Bounds on Photon-Orbit Instability in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity
summary: We derive a local upper bound on the coordinate-time Lyapunov exponent of unstable circular null orbits in static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity in $n\geq5$ dimensions with nonnegative Gauss--Bonnet coupling. On the regular Einstein branch, the tangential null energy condition suffices; no additional density-pressure inequality is required for the principal result. The bound retains the local matter-density contribution dictated by the field equations. Using the spherical mass relation, we express the departure of its dimensionless coefficient from the Einstein value $n-3$ in terms of the difference between the local density and the enclosed generalized Misner--Sharp mass per areal volume. This gives a sufficient density-contrast criterion for the Einstein optical bound to remain valid at nonzero coupling. Optical Gaussian curvature and tangential null convergence provide geometrical interpretations that distinguish radial tidal instability from the focusing of a null congruence. Vacuum solutions saturate the bound, while a Maxwell field with nonzero charge produces a strictly positive gap. The smooth Einstein limit and explicit vacuum and charged solutions provide consistency checks. A separate matter condition yields a density-free corollary. We also discuss consequences for strong-deflection lensing and test-field eikonal damping within their respective regimes of validity.

title: Finite temperature Fredholm determinants for dynamical correlation functions
summary: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants using effective form factors. The method expresses these asymptotics as a functional of an effective phase shift. We determine its two branches on either side of a quadratic stationary point and the transition profile joining them. The profile is expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. Its connection to the high-temperature Gaussian $β$ ensemble fixes the finite normalization, in agreement with an independent Riemann--Hilbert analysis. We also show that the leading exponential asymptotics suffice to recover the Euler-scale prediction of generalized hydrodynamics for the dynamical structure factor of hard rods.

title: Probing first-generation doublet vector-like leptons via single production at the 3 TeV CLIC
summary: The single production of first-generation $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ doublet vector-like leptons (VLLs) at the Compact Linear Collider (CLIC) with $\sqrt{s}=3~\mathrm{TeV}$ is studied. The neutral and charged VLL states are investigated through $e^+e^-\rightarrowν_e\bar N+\barν_eN$ and $e^+e^-\rightarrow e^\pm E^\mp$, respectively. The neutral VLL is searched for in the $N\rightarrow W^\mp e^\pm$ channel with $W^\pm\rightarrow jj$, leading to the $e^\pm+2j+\slashed{E}_T$ final state. The charged VLL is explored through $E^\pm\rightarrow e^\pm h$ ($h\rightarrow b\bar b$) and $E^\pm\rightarrow e^\pm Z$ ($Z\rightarrow q\bar q$), yielding the $e^+e^-+2b$ and $e^+e^-+2j$ signatures. Signal and background simulations include initial-state radiation, beamstrahlung, and detector effects. Cut-based analyses are performed for integrated luminosities of $1$, $3$, and $5~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$ to obtain the exclusion and discovery sensitivities in the VLL mass--mixing parameter space. The neutral-VLL channel gives the best sensitivity. At $1~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, the $2σ$ exclusion reaches $\varepsilon\simeq0.013$ at $M_N=1.3~\mathrm{TeV}$ and $\varepsilon\simeq0.065$ at $M_N=2.9~\mathrm{TeV}$, while the $5σ$ discovery reach corresponds to $\varepsilon\simeq0.02$--$0.10$. At $5~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, the charged-VLL channels probe masses up to about $2.9~\mathrm{TeV}$ and $2.8~\mathrm{TeV}$ in the $e^\pm h$ and $e^\pm Z$ modes, respectively. These results demonstrate that a 3 TeV CLIC can provide sensitive probes of first-generation doublet VLLs over a wide mass range, including scenarios with small VLL--electron mixing.

title: Retarded Green Function For Bopp--Podolsky Electrodynamics in Four-Dimensional De Sitter Spacetime
summary: We study classical Bopp--Podolsky (BP) electrodynamics on four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime, focusing on its transverse retarded Green function and gauge-invariant electromagnetic response. Because de Sitter spacetime is maximally symmetric, its vector Green functions admit a covariant expansion in a finite basis of invariant bitensors, with scalar coefficients depending only on the invariant separation. For conserved sources, the fourth-order field operator factorizes into Maxwell and massive-vector operators, yielding the BP retarded kernel as the difference of their transverse Green functions. Using the invariant bitensor decomposition, we reduce the propagator equations to a hypergeometric master equation and determine the distributional structure of its solution. The common leading short-distance singularity of the Maxwell and massive-vector sectors cancels, leaving a logarithmic master singularity and a softened vector-potential wavefront. After one curl, the gauge-invariant field-strength kernel contains a null-cone delta distribution and a regular timelike tail. The smooth Maxwell master tail is annihilated by the curl, so the interior electromagnetic tail is generated entirely by the massive sector. We also derive an exact horizon-regular static potential, demonstrate the cancellation of the Coulomb divergence, recover the flat-space BP potential, and formulate the generalized Gauss law. On global de Sitter spacetime, the compactness of the spatial sections requires the total charge to vanish; we implement this constraint using an antipodal charge configuration with smooth factorized initial data. The analysis is classical and does not assume a quantum Lee--Wick contour or a preferred de Sitter vacuum.

title: Neutrino Tridents and $W$-boson production at the Muon Collider
summary: Muon colliders are exceptionally intense sources of multi-TeV neutrinos, allowing even relatively small detectors to record large rates of neutrino interactions. In addition to serving as neutrino-ion collider for precision measurements of neutrino deep inelastic scattering, this setup allow to study even rare neutrino processes with at high statistics. In this study, we investigate the feasibility of measuring neutrino trident and on-shell W-boson production, predicting over one million trident events and one hundred thousand W-boson events in a 100 kg silicon-based active target over ten years and allowing to detect these processes for the first time. We further show that these measurements could constrain new vector and axial-vector interactions beyond projected DUNE sensitivities and provide unprecedented constraints on the high-x photon distribution through W-boson production near threshold. We also discuss strategies for signal-background discrimination and the resulting detector requirements.

title: Einstein Telescope: the triangle in a network and the impact of the relative orientation of detectors
summary: The geometrical configuration of the Einstein Telescope (ET) gravitational-wave observatory is one the most important design choices to be made for this future scientific facility. Two baseline configurations are currently being considered, a single triangle or 2 distant L-shaped detectors tilted by about $45^{\circ}$. In this document we present a study of the scientific performance of the ET baseline configurations in both stand-alone mode and in the presence of either an L-shaped Cosmic Explorer detector with 40-km long arms located in the United States or the existing LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA network. We also include in the study an alternative ET configuration, which is currently not being considered and consists of a triangle plus a distant L-shaped detector. We find that in stand-alone mode this alternative configuration performs significantly better than the other two in both the compact binary coalescence and stochastic gravitational wave background scientific cases. The differences in performance between the ET configurations are reduced in the presence of the considered, additional non-ET detectors. We also show that the impact of possible correlated noise in co-located detectors on the stochastic gravitational-wave background performance can be addressed with the addition of extra detectors. Finally, we study the impact on the ET scientific performance of the relative orientation of the future detectors in the network. We find that, while the configurations that include a triangular ET detector are basically insensitive to this orientation, a balanced compromise for the ET configuration consisting of two L-shaped detectors could be represented by a tilt angle between the two detectors of about $30^{\circ}$.

title: Spacetimes of maximal proper acceleration and muon mean lifetime
summary: In this paper, it is shown that in spacetimes of maximal proper acceleration, there is a reduction of the mean lifetime of the muon. We consider several candidates for the maximal proper acceleration. For all of them, the induced corrections are small, but for the case when the maximal proper acceleration is identified with the Schwinger's acceleration, the effect is detectable in future muon collider facilities.

title: Concurrence Dynamics in Self-Gravitating Mixed Neutrinos
summary: We study the entanglement generated by Newtonian self-gravity in a two-particle system of mixed neutrinos and quantify it by means of the concurrence. Starting from the gravitational coupling between the mass operators, we show that the two-particle Hamiltonian splits into local single-particle terms and an effective Ising interaction in the mass basis, the latter being solely responsible for the generation of correlations. For initially separable flavor states the concurrence is obtained in closed analytic form: it oscillates between zero and a maximum fixed by the mixing angle alone, while the gravitational coupling sets the recurrence time. We further establish a one-to-one correspondence between the concurrence and the reduced-state purity previously derived for this model, thus providing an independent quantum-information description of the same gravitationally induced correlations. Finally, we show that the concurrence does not depend on the Majorana phase, so that Dirac and Majorana parametrizations yield identical entanglement dynamics. These results isolate the genuinely entangling sector of the gravitational evolution and provide a compact analytic characterization of gravity-induced quantum correlations in mixed neutrino systems.

title: A first order nonabelian antisymmetric tensor model with hidden higher symmetry
summary: We present a nonabelian complex self-dual antisymmetric tensor model, with gauged internal symmetry, comprising a complex multiplet of massless self-dual antisymmetric tensor fields and its conjugate (interacting with massless Yang-Mills gauge fields). We build the model at the classical level, via a first order formulation, assigning local fields to a component expansion over the Dirac algebra and a basis of internal matrices, with Lorentz and gauge invariance ensured by tracing, and applying an appropriate bilinear form. The full expansion requires auxiliary place-holder fields, which are not potentials, but become curvatures (field strengths) after elimination via their algebraic equations of motion. The component expansion over the Dirac algebra is closed under multiplication by additional internal matrices, which are not gauge group generators, but mix internal components, and link auxiliary curvatures with potentials. The model is shown to be invariant under such transformations, and thus possesses a type of hidden internal symmetry. We analyze the specific case of gauge group $SU(2)\! \times \! U(1)$, and as higher symmetry candidates, we consider both the Lie group $SU(3)$ and the Lie superalgebra $SU(2/1)$ (with the additional matrices acting via Lie brackets, or graded Lie brackets, respectively).

title: Lepton Flavour Universality in Semileptonic $\bar B_{(s)} \to D_{(s)}^{(\ast)}$ Transitions
summary: Using continuum Schwinger function methods, we deliver parameter-free pointwise predictions for the complete set of twelve Standard Model (SM) $\bar B_{(s)} \to D_{(s)}^{(\ast)}$, i.e., $b\to c$, semileptonic transition form factors on the entire kinematically accessible domain. Therewith, we calculate SM theory values for the decay-rate ratios of $τ$ and $μ$ final states: $\{ R(D) \, , \, R(D)^\ast \} = \{ 0.290(11) \, , \, 0.267(5) \}$, $\{ R(D_{s}) \, , \, R(D_{s}^{\ast}) \} = \{ 0.283(11) \, , \, 0.251(5) \}$. The former is consistent with an existing average of SM estimates, but disagrees with the experimental average by $2.8σ$. Comparing transitions with light quark and strange quark spectators, we find a $2.3σ$ signal for violation of SU$(3)$ flavour symmetry, expressed at the 5% level in $D_{(s)}^\ast$ final states. It is induced by Higgs boson couplings into the strong interaction and modulated by phenomena deriving from emergent features of the strong interaction.

title: Parton and nuclear dynamics at large $x$: the CJ26 global QCD analysis
comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. Proceedings of DIS2026, Bologna, Italy, 4-8 May 2026
summary: We present the new CTEQ-JLab global QCD analysis, called CJ26, that simultaneously fits parton distribution functions of the proton and nuclear effects in deuteron targets. This work includes, for the first time in a global fit, the full set of JLab 6 GeV inclusive DIS measurements and the first published JLab 12 GeV data. The analysis focuses on the large-$x$ region, and carefully treats the interplay between higher-twist effects and off-shell corrections in low-energy proton and deuteron target data. We discuss their effect on quark and gluon distributions, and highlight the importance of quantifying the experimental correlated systematic uncertainty to achieve fits of the highest accuracy. We also outline how upcoming data may help unravel the nuclear and partonic dynamics in light nuclei. The extracted next-to-leading order parton distributions are available on the CJ web pages in LHAPDF format for general use, accompanied by leading- and higher-twist structure functions calculated with the simultaneously fitted PDFs, higher-twist corrections, and off-shell corrections. This write up clarifies several points that became clearer while finalizing the CJ26 paper and can be read as a companion to the latter.

title: Mathematical framework for simulation of non-perturbative cavity optomechanics with plate-like dielectrics
summary: Cavity optomechanical models typically treat a sensor either as a perturbative polarizable object in a pre-existing optical field, or solve the field at a fixed equilibrium and linearize in a fixed optical-mode basis. Neither self-consistently determines the spatially resolved cavity field, the optical force, the mechanical equilibrium, and the back-action when a finite-thickness dielectric plate intercepts the entire optical mode and restructures the intracavity field. In this companion paper to [1], we develop that treatment by extending the vacuum two-photon formalism to finite-thickness planar dielectrics, incorporating their Fresnel reflection, internal propagation, optical forces, and mechanical back-action directly into the field equations. We derive the carrier and sideband transfer functions needed to describe the coupled optical-mechanical system, including optomechanical cooling and the response to external perturbations. The result is a systematic starting point for calculating detector response and noise budgets for cavity experiments with intracavity dielectrics, including gravitational wave detectors deploying levitated sensors.

title: Haagerup conformal field theory at central charge eight
summary: We construct a chiral algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside the lattice vertex operator algebra $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$. It is generated by two commuting affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ current algebras at levels $1$ and $39$, the stress tensor of the lattice theory, and a single weight-two field built from three lattice exponentials. We announce that $U$ is strongly rational and completely unitary, and that $Rep(U)$ is equivalent, as a unitary ribbon category, to the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category $\mathcal{H}_3$. Its characters are the $γ=0$ Evans--Gannon vector. From $U$ we obtain a diagonal full CFT, and also a holomorphic $E_8$ extension on which $\mathcal{H}_3$ acts by topological defects.

title: New topological phase transitions in $κ$-deformed $φ^4$ lattice models
summary: This paper explores topological phase transitions in the momentum space of the $κ$-deformed $φ^4$ lattice model within the mean-field approximation. We show that the double-well structure of the momentum space gives rise to degenerate momentum states at high energies and that this change is marked by a phase transition. We investigate this transition using both numerical and analytical methods, with the analytical approach based primarily on singularity theory. Our numerical analysis shows that the energy at which the topological phase transition occurs is related to the noncommutative parameter by the simple power law $E \sim 1/α^{4}$. By mapping the constant-energy-level surface to the $A_{3}$ singularity, we obtain the same result analytically. We also present results unique to noncommutative systems, showing that the fraction of particles in degenerate momentum states has a nonzero commutative limit. As a nonperturbative effect, this result provides a testable prediction for the existence of noncommutative spacetime.

title: Regular-Zero Drinfeld-Sokolov Charges in Doubled Four-Dimensional Chern-Simons Theory
summary: We study classical local conserved charges obtained after finite-defect reduction of doubled four-dimensional Chern--Simons theory. At a finite simple zero, the inhomogeneous derivative term in the affine gauge transformation induced by the twist function vanishes, so the residue evaluations of the two Gaudin currents transform by the ordinary adjoint action. For each simple ideal, we use the Evans-compatible invariant tensors of the principal Drinfeld--Sokolov hierarchy as external algebraic input, construct local circle integrals, and treat the same-zero, distinct-zero, and mixed sectors separately, proving pairwise Poisson commutativity. Under the explicit assumptions of Stedman's simple-pole/simple-zero boundary Hamiltonian, the periodic trivial-monodromy sector, and boundary weights independent of phase-space variables, the reduced Hamiltonian decomposes term by term into finite-pole, infinity, finite-zero, and residual first-class-constraint contributions, which yields conservation of the constructed charges. We distinguish the finite-defect reduced space, the extended space carrying the residual constraint, and the physical quotient. The result is a conditional existence statement for a classical local Abelian Poisson subalgebra; we make no claim of functional independence, maximality, or Liouville completeness. Extensions to higher-order zeros and nontrivial monodromy sectors are outside the scope of this work.

title: Parton distribution functions and strong coupling constant: MSHT
comment: 30 pages, 8 figures. Written in 2025 for Physics Reports review article, now published
summary: We present an overview of the MSHT family of global PDF fits. We describe the underlying methodology, including parameterisation choice, theoretical inputs and datasets included in the fit. We describe the impact of recent theoretical advances in the inclusion of higher order QCD and EW corrections on the fit and their implications for phenomenology. We discuss recent methodological improvements and ongoing studies relating to closure tests of the parameterisation flexibility and the inclusion of errors on errors for experimental data. We in addition discuss recent results on the determination of the strong coupling from the MSHT fits.

title: A No-Go Theorem for Nonspherical Bounces with a Single Negative Mode
summary: False vacuum decay is conventionally described by a spherically symmetric bounce with a single negative fluctuation mode. This raises a fundamental question: can the single negative mode requirement itself enforce spherical symmetry, independently of action minimization? For a single real scalar field with a smooth potential in flat spacetime, we rigorously prove that every localized nonspherical saddle with zero initial velocity has at least three negative modes. Additional reflection symmetries further tighten these bounds, as illustrated in a sextic scalar model. Our findings exclude nonspherical bounce candidates with a single negative mode, providing a complementary spectral foundation for the spherical bounce description of false vacuum decay.

title: Signature of GW from the Hidden Sector in light of the Recent LZ Event
summary: The LZ collaboration has recently reported a single nuclear-recoil event at $E_R=248\pm23_\text{stat}\pm23_\text{sys}$ keV, observed in a 2.84 tonne-year exposure with a local significance of $3.4σ$, pointing towards an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation. We explain this event within a gauged $U(1)_X$ hidden-sector model, spontaneously broken by a singlet scalar whose vacuum expectation value (VEV) gives rise to: \textit{(i)} gauge boson mass, \textit{(ii)} a small Majorana mass for the vector-like singlet fermion, the DM candidate, charged under the new symmetry, which splits the fermion into two pseudo-Dirac states (mass splitting proportional to the scalar VEV) thus resulting in a purely off-diagonal vector current, \textit{(iii)} the frequency and the amplitude of the GW signal arising from the hidden sector symmetry breaking via first-order phase transition (FOPT). The symmetry-breaking scale thus provides a multi-messenger probe connecting terrestrial direct-detection kinematics at the LZ and early-universe FOPT thermodynamics while obtaining thermal DM relic abundance. We delineate the viable parameter space compatible with the LZ event, correct relic density, and detectable GW signals in the low frequency regimes at future interferometers like $μ{\rm ARES}$ and THEIA while satisfying existing cosmological, astrophysical, and terrestrial bounds.

title: Hamiltonian analysis of disformally coupled fermions in scalar-tensor theories
summary: We study disformal transformations of $\mathcal{N}$ scalar fields coupled to a Dirac fermion. The resulting axial coupling generically introduces higher derivatives in the scalar field equations of motion; for field-dependent free functions, these are absent if and only if the disformal transformation acts along a single field-space direction. We show that these higher derivatives do not signal an Ostrogradsky ghost. After the transformation, the fermion registers the derivatives of the matter-frame tetrad only through the axial current, so that every coupling to the derivatives of the scalar fields multiplies a fermion bilinear, which is Grassmann even and nilpotent. Such terms do not contribute to the body of the constraint matrix, and at each level of the Grassmann expansion the field equations are linear, with the principal part of the theory without fermions. Through a Hamiltonian analysis, we show that the number of degrees of freedom is that of the bosonic theory plus that of the fermion, both in the Einstein frame, for free functions depending on the scalar fields and their kinetic matrix, and for minimally coupled fermions in multi-field DHOST theories. The same mechanism applies to disformal transformations with higher derivatives of a single scalar field, for which fermions impose no condition beyond those required by bosonic matter.

title: Analytic Brill wave initial data with trapped surfaces
comment: 25 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables; Python code as ancillary files
summary: Since Brill's work of 1959, the conformal factor of finite-amplitude Brill waves, the axisymmetric and time-symmetric vacuum initial data on $\mathbb{R}^3$ that describe pure gravitational radiation, has been obtained only numerically, up to the most recent studies. Here an explicit one-parameter family of such data is constructed: the first explicit real-analytic, non-trivial, asymptotically flat vacuum initial data with trivial topology and a single end. The free metric function is a closed-form combination of elementary functions and a dilogarithm. The data have the toroidal conformal symmetry of Beig and Husa, and a change of variable of Natanzon type reduces every mode equation to the Gauss hypergeometric equation, so that the conformal factor is a series with explicit Gamma-function coefficients. The quantities that have so far required numerical work are thereby obtained exactly. A ground-state identity gives a sharp existence criterion: complete, asymptotically flat data exist precisely for $k<k_c=0.8048016772\ldots$, and the explicit series is identified with the unique variational solution. The ADM mass is an absolutely convergent digamma series, with $m/a=πk^2/10+O(k^3)$ for small amplitudes and an explicit residue at its critical divergence. Sufficiently strong waves contain trapped surfaces: it is proved that for $k$ close to $k_c$ the rescaled conformal factor converges to an explicit function and explicit tori and spheres become outer trapped, so that the data contain an apparent horizon. A numerical search, restricted to equatorially symmetric star-shaped surfaces, finds marginally trapped (minimal) spheres, which appear in a fold near $k=0.7670$. No thin-torus or weak-field approximation is used.

title: Yang-Baxter deformed sigma models on $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathrm{SO}(N)$
summary: We study Yang--Baxter deformations of two-dimensional sigma models on compact symmetric spaces $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathrm{SO}(N)$, with particular emphasis on their ultraviolet behavior. We claim that the ultraviolet fixed point is described by the $\mathrm{SO}(N,\mathbb C)/\mathrm{SO}(N,\mathbb R)$ non-compact WZW model together with $N-1$ compact free bosons. We determine the leading correction to this fixed point and identify it with the perturbation generated by the corresponding screening currents. We also extend our construction to the broader class of symmetric spaces of maximal rank.

title: From Earth to Mars and Beyond: AI-Driven Cosmic-Ray Validation and Prediction with CorsikaAgent
summary: We calculate the sea-level cosmic-ray muon flux with CORSIKA and develop CorsikaAgent, an auditable large-language-model-based system for configuring, executing, and validating air-shower simulations, and for predicting particle fluxes in unexplored environments. The physics calculation uses proton primaries described by the solar-minimum spectrum of Papini et al., with UrQMD at low interaction energies and either Sibyll 2.3e or QGSJET-III at high energies. The predicted momentum spectra at approximately 0 and 75 degrees are compared with experimental measurements of the atmospheric muon flux and with commonly used analytic parametrizations. The two interaction-model configurations give similar spectra and describe the principal momentum and zenith-angle dependences of the data. The agent independently reconstructs the same observable through a different sampling strategy and keeps every steering card, executable, seed, log, and analysis script bound to the result it produced; its output is consistent with the direct calculation at the level resolved by the present comparison. Transferred to Mars, the workflow reproduces the CORSIKA 8 benchmark, and transferred to Venus it produces the first prediction of the surface muon flux, an environment for which no measurement exists. The agent thus extends the workflow from auditable reproduction to first-principles prediction: it autonomously reconfigures the simulation(atmosphere, magnetic field, electric field)for new environments, while the proton-only primary model, limited high-momentum statistics, and an incomplete systematic-uncertainty treatment bound the physical precision that can currently be claimed.

title: About P-adic Numbers and Professor Igor Volovich on the Occasion of his 80th Anniversary
comment: To appear in the 2026 Proceedings of the"New Horizons in Mathematical Physics" published by the Steklov Mathematical Institute, Moscow
summary: We recall a 1987 paper written by Volovich and our subsequent work with Okada which established the Feyman rules for the p-adic string and the related non-local field theory which found diverse physical applications. We add some memories of visits to Moscow during 1989-91.

title: HEPTABench: A framework for portable and controlled agentic evaluations in high energy physics
comment: 45 pages, 10 figures, 4 tables. Public code available
summary: Quantifying the capability and reliability of agentic systems in high-energy physics (HEP) requires repeated evaluations under controlled configurations. Establishing whether changes to models, tools, or harnesses improve performance also requires these components to be varied independently. We present the High Energy Physics Tool-and-Agent Benchmarking (HEPTABench) framework for portable and controlled evaluations of agentic systems, with separately configurable tasks, scaffolding, models, providers, harnesses, and domain capabilities. The framework combines HEP benchmark tasks and scientific rubrics with experiment execution and versioned tool interfaces. To support inspection, reproducibility, and post-hoc grading, the framework prioritizes recording and reporting complete experiment specifications, agent trajectories, and experiment artifacts. We demonstrate the framework in two benchmark campaigns. The first campaign evaluates a forward long-lived-particle reach calculation across four frontier coding-agent systems, comparing their built-in coding tools with the same tools supplemented by HEP domain tools. We show that including these HEP domain tools improves numerical accuracy and reduces trial-to-trial dispersion for every tested system. In a complementary campaign covering eight symbolic two-body decay tasks, we show that adding symbolic domain tools increases the fraction of successful trials for Claude Haiku 4.5 from $8\%$ to $79\%$, while GPT-5.5 succeeds in every trial with built-in tools alone. Through systematic evaluation of agentic systems, HEPTABench enables the identification of factors that improve the accuracy and reliability of their scientific work.

title: Black holes with dark matter halos and a positive cosmological constant: Energy conditions and signatures
summary: We study static, spherically symmetric black holes surrounded by dark matter halos in the presence of a positive cosmological constant. Assuming vanishing radial pressure, we derive the constraints imposed by the null, weak, strong, and dominant energy conditions on the halo matter. The halo is confined to a finite radial interval separated from both horizons, and the total mass is bounded above by the Nariai value. We construct a Hernquist-type profile and study black hole images, showing that a positive cosmological constant can substantially change the images. We also compute scalar quasinormal modes of the Hernquist-type spacetime. When the dark matter mass is sufficiently small, the relative difference of a selected mode is approximately linear in the compactness of the matter halo, i.e., the ratio of mass parameter $M_{\text{DM}}$ and scale parameter $a$, with a coefficient that depends on the cosmological constant.

title: Beyond the circle: current algebras, geometry and higher gauge structures
comment: Contribution to the Proceedings for the conference Frontiers of Lie Theory: Computational Aspects and Applications, Bedlewo, 28.09 - 04.10, 2025, 20 pages
summary: Replacing the circle by a manifold leads to current Lie algebras and their central and derivation extensions. We separate the coefficient algebra, harmonic analysis and geometric data. Differentials modulo exact forms describe central extensions; divergence-free vector fields give explicit cocycles, whose compatible derivations satisfy a stabilizer equation. Compact examples include the three-sphere and its current--Virasoro extension. We also explain the analytic qualifications for SL(2,R) and its symmetric space and the role of transported multiplication in soft geometries. The recent harmonic constructions of Campoamor-Stursberg, Marrani and Rausch de Traubenberg are compared with the cohomological work of Coquereaux, Frappat, Ragoucy and Sorba and Castellani's loop geometry and infinite-dimensional free differential algebras. A coefficient-algebra construction connects currents to higher brackets and clarifies the additional requirements of a dynamical theory. For Lie algebras of order F, central extensions obey coupled binary and symmetric F-ary conditions, with explicit examples and obstructions.

title: Two-pion source analysis in small to large systems at SPS energies
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, proceedings of the 18th Workshop on Particle Correlations and Femtoscopy (WPCF 2026), Budapest, Hungary, May 18 - 22, 2026, submitted to the International Journal of Modern Physics A, Thematic Issue on Paritcle Correlations and Femtoscopy
summary: Over the past decade, femtoscopic measurements using Lévy-stable source functions have been carried out in collision systems ranging from small to large at SPS, RHIC, and LHC energies. In recent years, these have been accompanied by a number of phenomenological studies of the same systems and energies. We contribute to this line of work by investigating the shape of two-pion pair-source distributions in central $^7$Be+$^9$Be and $^{129}$Xe+$^{139}$La collisions simulated with the UrQMD model in cascade mode. To make the comparison with measurements meaningful, kinematic selections similar to the experimental ones are applied to the simulated events and particles. One-dimensional Lévy fits are performed, and the resulting source parameters are studied as functions of pair transverse mass, collision energy, and system size. We find that the simulated sources are well described by Lévy distributions in all systems considered, which offers a common phenomenological picture of the space-time structure of pion emission. Finally, we compare our findings with results from an intermediate system, Ar+Sc. The results serve as a purely hadronic reference for past and upcoming femtoscopic measurements of the NA61/SHINE experiment.

title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
summary: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.

title: Exact radial stability threshold for a Minkowski-Schwarzschild thin shell
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Submitted to Physics Letters B
summary: We study the stability of a thin shell of ordinary matter that separates a flat interior from a Schwarzschild exterior, which is the simplest model of a subluminal warp drive. The matter content of the shell is fixed by the junction conditions and satisfies all the standard energy conditions except very close to the horizon. For a shell made of causal matter we find an exact radius below which it cannot be stable under radial perturbations. We then place a black hole inside the shell and show that this radius grows with the black hole mass, so that the flat interior is the most favourable case. Since such shells are known to be unstable to non-radial perturbations, our result marks the boundary of the region in which any stabilising mechanism would have to operate.

title: Classical and quantum scattering of massive Klein--Gordon fields in asymptotically flat spacetimes
summary: We use microlocal tools to define distinguished incoming and outgoing vacuum states of the quantum theory of massive Klein--Gordon fields in non-trapping asymptotically flat spacetimes, including radiative perturbations of Minkowski space. The asymptotic vacuum states satisfy the Hadamard condition, and the incoming and outgoing particle representations are unitarily equivalent, or in other words the quantum S-matrix is well-defined. These results are based on a description of scattering of classical fields which keeps track of the asymptotic distinction between positive- and negative-frequency solutions of the Klein--Gordon equation. Our emphasis is on developing the theory without recourse to explicit asymptotics for classical waves.

title: Conserved-charge diffusion in hot and dense QCD matter
comment: 11 pages, 7 captioned figures. Submitted for publication
summary: We study the coupled diffusion of baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness in hot and dense quark matter using a three-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model with self-consistently generated constituent quark masses. The complete diffusion matrix is evaluated within a relaxation-time kinetic approach, including its diagonal and off-diagonal components. We find that the off-diagonal transport coefficients exhibit distinct temperature and baryon-chemical-potential dependence associated with the flavor-dependent composition of the charge carriers. We further investigate generalized charge diffusivities and mobilities obtained from the corresponding susceptibilities. At finite baryon chemical potential, the baryon and strangeness mobility scales cross, reflecting the different density dependence of their transport coefficients and susceptibilities. The results provide model benchmarks for coupled conserved-charge transport in baryon-rich QCD matter.

title: Event Generation for Neutrino and Muon DIS at the LHC
summary: Neutrinos and muons produced in the forward direction of LHC collisions and detected by the FASER and SND@LHC experiments enable a comprehensive deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) programme, covering both neutral and charged currents, at TeV energies. This programme aims to provide stringent constraints on proton and nuclear structure as well as on hadron fragmentation, and to offer novel insight into neutrino interactions at the highest energies achieved in a laboratory. Realising this potential requires accurate and precise simulations of neutral- and charged-current DIS. We systematically compare the predictions of NLO general-purpose Monte Carlo (MC) event generators for neutrino- and muon-initiated DIS at the LHC (Sherpa, Herwig7, and POWHEG) against analytical structure-function calculations (YADISM) and dedicated neutrino simulation packages (GENIE, NuWro, GiBUU). Within this framework, we quantify the role of higher-order QCD corrections, (nuclear) parton distribution functions (PDFs), parton shower and hadronisation modelling, and QED radiation both for inclusive observables and for the FASER fiducial selections. We also present representative applications to the FASER neutrino programme: comparisons with its most recent data from the emulsion and electronic sub-detectors, a study of strange PDF sensitivity in the dimuon final state, and predictions for charged-hadron production in semi-inclusive DIS. Our analysis highlights the agreement of modern event generators for inclusive and differential DIS observables once common settings are adopted, while differences remain for observables sensitive to the hadronic final state.

title: Chiral partners of strange doubly heavy baryons: Mass relations and decay predictions after the 2026 LHCb discoveries
comment: Extended version based on presentation at the CERN workshop "Implications and prospects of exotic hadrons at LHCb" (October 4-7, 2026)
summary: Three spectacular LHCb measurements in 2026---the observations of $Ω_{cc}^{+}$, $Ξ_{cc}^{+}$, and the beauty-strange structure $B_{s0}^{*}(5700)^0$---make possible an experimentally constrained analysis of chiral partners of strange doubly heavy baryons. The doubly charmed masses test the earlier Ma--Harada prediction and support a compact, internally S-wave $cc$ color source. We combine this comparison with the heavy-quark--diquark hyperfine relation and with chiral gaps from the theory of chiral doublers, to construct consistent $ccs$ and $bbs$ parity multiplets and a conditional extension to $bcs$. Under meson-to-baryon parity-gap transfer, the $349$ MeV input from the $D_s$ sector gives negative-parity $ccs$ targets near $4.075$ and $4.183$ GeV. The separate $332$ MeV input from the $B_s$ sector fixes the $bbs$ partner masses relative to their unknown ground-state mass, conditional on the new beauty-strange state's chiral-partner assignment. We relate the differences of hyperfine splittings in the two parity sectors of mesons and baryons, and identify equal reduced single-pion widths, an E1 reduced-width ratio $1:8:4:5$, and a kaon selection rule whose leading predictions contain no new transition parameters. Absolute widths are estimated by matching the published Bardeen--Eichten--Hill and Harada--Rho--Sasaki meson calculations to a common convention. In the reference calculation, all members of the predicted $ccs$ and $bbs$ multiplets are narrow. In the proposed $Ω_{QQ}π^0$ and $Ω_{QQ}γ$ searches at LHCb, these states are expected to produce peaks dominated by detector resolution, allowing their masses and decay patterns to be investigated even when their intrinsic widths remain unresolved. The upper charm state is above kaon threshold but protected in the spectator limit.

title: Out-of-time-order hydrodynamics and scrambling
summary: Hydrodynamics as an effective field theory (EFT) has been immensely successful for predicting the behaviour of time-ordered correlation functions in the long-time, large-distance regime. In this paper, we analyse the predictions of hydrodynamics for scrambling as probed by out-of-time order correlators (OTOCs). To do so, we consider an all-derivative order generalisation of the Schwinger-Keldysh EFT of hydrodynamics extended to a four-fold time contour required to capture OTOCs. A crucial ingredient of the construction is a local SL(2,R) symmetry, which has previously been suggested as a mechanism for scrambling. We also derive this exact EFT from the microscopic formulation of the maximally chaotic low-temperature limit of the SYK lattice, thereby determining all transport coefficients for this model. As a novel application, we compute the OTOC of energy currents, find that its exponential growth saturates the chaos bound, and match it to expectations based on a shockwave (or scramblon) effective description. Our work shows that the universality of hydrodynamics degrees of freedom extends beyond traditional time-ordered correlators to more complex observables such as OTOCs.

The asymptotic vacuum states satisfy the Hadamard condition, and the incoming and outgoing particle representations are unitarily equivalent, or in other words the quantum S-matrix is well-defined. These results are based on a description of scattering of classical fields which keeps track of the asymptotic distinction between positive- and negative-frequency solutions of the Klein--Gordon equation. Our emphasis is on developing the theory without recourse to explicit asymptotics for classical waves.

title: Quasiperiodic oscillations as probes of rotating black holes in exponential dark matter environments
summary: We construct the rotating counterpart of a black hole embedded in a dark-matter halo with the exponential-sphere profile $ρ=ρ_0e^{-r/r_0}$, using the Newman--Janis algorithm in the Azreg-Aïnou form, and study its imprints on test-particle motion and quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs). We derive closed-form orbital and epicyclic frequencies valid for any Kerr-like metric with a mass function and show that, to first order, the halo enters them only through its central density, acting as an effective cosmological constant $Λ_{eff}=8πρ_0$; the corrections are therefore universal for all cored profiles. The halo moves the innermost stable circular orbit outward and produces an outer boundary of stable orbits, while the sign of the frequency shift depends on the assumed equation of state of the halo. Fitting the relativistic precession model to the simultaneous QPO triplets of GRO~J1655$-$40 and XTE~J1859+226 with Markov-chain Monte Carlo sampling yields spins and emission radii consistent with Kerr and $ρ_0M^2<2.9\times10^{-5}$ and $3.0\times10^{-5}$ (95\%), respectively. In physical units these limits exclude only ultra-dense dark cores, $ρ_0\gtrsim10^{11}$~g\,cm$^{-3}$.

title: Supersymmetric Observables from Surface Defect Anomalies in 4d and 6d SCFTs
summary: We study the contributions of half-BPS surface defects to supersymmetric Casimir energy and the universal logarithmic term of supersymmetric Rényi entropy in four- and six-dimensional SCFTs. Using equivariant integration of defect anomaly polynomials and its extension to supersymmetric Rényi backgrounds, we obtain closed expressions for these observables in terms of defect 't Hooft anomalies. For Gukov--Witten defects preserving transverse rotations in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super Yang--Mills theories, both observables depend on a single R-symmetry anomaly. For $\mathcal{N} = (0, 4)$ defects in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (1, 0)$ theories, additional terms arise from the gravitational anomaly. We provide complementary checks using chiral algebras, five-dimensional localization, and holographic probe branes at large $N$, while localized chiral fermions reproduce the gravitational-anomaly contributions. The framework also recovers Wilson-surface results in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (2, 0)$ theories.

title: Invisible Decays of the $Z$ in Portal Matter Models at Tera-Z
summary: Searches for new contributions to the invisible width of the $Z$, $ΔΓ_{inv}$, can be used to provide model-dependent constraints on new physics that may arise from an unknown dark sector. In the vector portal setup considered here it is shown that loops of portal matter (PM) fields, having both Standard Model (SM) and dark sector quantum numbers, can lead to new contributions to $ΔΓ_{inv}$ that satisfy current experimental constraints while being simultaneously accessible to measurements at the future Tera-Z. Such PM fields, which here take the form of vector-like fermions, are well known to be able to induce kinetic mixing (KM) between the SM and dark photons (DP) at low energies. This analysis is performed within a simplified version of a previously examined `$E_6-$like' setup that predicts a calculable value for the strength of KM in a phenomenologically interesting range. On the other hand, owing to the constraint on the invisible branching fraction of the Higgs, the tree-level mixing of the SM and a weak isosinglet dark Higgs fields yields a value of $ΔΓ_{inv}$ which is far too small to be observable. A similar result holds for the shift in the $Z$'s invisible width induced by the mass and/or KM of the $Z$ with the light DP which then subsequently decays to dark matter. On the other hand, PM models wherein the light dark Higgs carries a significant admixture of a $T_3\neq 0$ weak isospin component are shown to already violate existing $ΔΓ_{inv}$ constraints in the absence of parameter tuning. Future measurements of $ΔΓ_{inv}$ can thus play an important role in providing indirect constraints on dark sector interactions and PM model building, in particular, on PM loops not necessarily associated with the generation of KM of the DP with the corresponding SM field.

title: Metric and dilaton information from high-overtone quasinormal modes of analytic Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton black holes
summary: Black-hole interiors are hidden from exterior observers, yet their geometry can enter the high-overtone spectrum of linear perturbations. We study how this spectrum encodes metric and supporting-matter information in analytic Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton black holes. Coupling a neutral spectator to the dilaton at fixed UV dimension provides a matter-sensitive channel alongside the momentum response. For real-endpoint spacelike connections, the momentum response and mass-label dependence separate the metric exponents from the signed dilaton slope. Near the causal threshold, a complex endpoint controls the spectral family: the mass profiles approach a common value, producing a shared fractional correction, while regular propagation retains label dependence. This mechanism is present at criticality without an inner horizon and continues locally into timelike interiors. Exterior numerical spectra support the reconstruction and the leading complex-endpoint responses. Local scaling and probe coupling set the candidate responses, while wave connection determines their imprint on the exterior spectrum.

title: Pseudo-spectral methods in gravitational lensing: Spin precession in loop quantum black hole spacetimes
comment: 24 pages, 5 figures in main texts, 1 illustration figure in appendix; comments welcome
summary: Gravitational lensing is usually treated as an initial value problem: for a given impact parameter of an unbound orbit, one computes the resulting deflection angle. In this paper we advocate the inverse point of view. For a prescribed deflection angle, the orbit is selected by two boundary conditions at spatial infinity, so that the lensing problem becomes a well-defined two-point boundary value problem, with the impact parameter playing the role of a nonlinear eigenvalue. We show that pseudo-spectral methods based on Chebyshev collocation solve this boundary value problem accurately at modest computational cost, and that the parallel transport equations governing the spin precession of the particle reduce to a single linear system on the same grid. As a concrete application, we compute the spin precession of massive particles in backward scattering off two black hole spacetimes from loop quantum gravity: the covariant effective metric and the self-dual loop quantum black hole. All equations are written for a general static, spherically symmetric line element with three free functions, so that both spacetimes are handled on the same footing. We find that the quantum corrections are most pronounced for slowly moving particles, while in the ultra-relativistic limit the universal spin flip is always recovered.
